x: Jhum (shifting cultivation) is the North-East practice and the Khasis of Meghalaya practise it; Bhotiyas are transhumant herders, Todas are pastoral, Santhals are settled cultivators.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography 05 p.1 (Jhum – North-East)

x: Mixed farming means growing crops and also rearing animals together; growing several crops at once is mixed cropping, not mixed farming.
Karnataka released India's first State Research, Development and Innovation Policy at the Bengaluru Tech Summit (Nov 2022), with a Karnataka State Research Foundation to drive it.
source: gktoday.in/karnataka-research-development-and-innovation-policy; deccanherald.com (Karnataka to get nation's first R&D policy)

from_notes_src: app notes 4:81 (sub 9); OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography 05 p.5
x: The hot, humid lower Gangetic plain (West Bengal) is the paddy and jute belt; wheat and cotton need cooler or drier conditions.
source: app notes 4:81 (sub 9); OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography 05 p.5

x: The ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR, 1999) is at Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh), not Kanpur, which has the pulses institute.
The Central (now National) Rice Research Institute is at Cuttack, Odisha; the Indian Institute of Rice Research is at Hyderabad.
ICRISAT has its headquarters at Patancheru near Hyderabad.
CRIDA (Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture, ICAR) is at Hyderabad; Jhansi has the grassland and fodder institute, Jodhpur CAZRI.
The Indian Institute of Pulses Research is at Kanpur, not Lucknow.
The Indian Institute of Vegetable Research is at Varanasi; Kanpur has the pulses institute.
The Upper Gangetic Plain zone covers central and western UP; its irrigation intensity is about 131% and cropping intensity about 144-145%, so both statements are correct.
source: Planning Commission agro-climatic zone data as given in insightsonindia.com Agro-Climatic Regions and eagri AGRO101 lec07

x: CRIDA is at Hyderabad.
CRIDA (ICAR) is at Hyderabad.
NBSS&LUP divides India into 20 agro-ecological zones; 15 is the Planning Commission's count of agro-climatic zones.
India has 20 agro-ecological zones (NBSS&LUP); do not confuse them with the 15 agro-climatic zones.
Anaemia is caused mainly by iron deficiency, which cuts haemoglobin; calcium, magnesium and zinc deficiencies cause other disorders.
source: NCERT Class 12 Biology / standard GS fact

x: Rice tungro is a viral disease caused by two viruses together (rice tungro bacilliform and spherical viruses), spread by green leafhoppers; Xanthomonas causes bacterial blight and Pyricularia causes blast.

from_notes_src: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography 05 p.8 (pulses fix nitrogen)
x: Pea is a legume whose root nodules host Rhizobium, which fixes atmospheric nitrogen; rice, wheat and maize are cereals and cannot do this.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography 05 p.8 (pulses fix nitrogen)

from_notes_src: UPSC CSE 2012 official key; printed explanation
x: Cowpea and green gram serve as pulse, fodder and green manure; pigeon pea is mainly a pulse with a long duration, so it is not a green-manure crop (UPSC 2012 key: 1 and 2 only).
source: UPSC CSE 2012 official key; printed explanation

x: Mahi Sugandha is a basmati (scented) rice variety.
Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are the biofertiliser of paddy fields.
Mahi Kanchan is a maize from the Banswara (Mahi) maize research station of MPUAT and RCB 911 is a Rajasthan bajra hybrid, so maize and bajra respectively.
source: printed key, not verified; printed explanation (RPSC 2023)
evidence: web search found no official release record

x: Cowpea and green gram are used as pulse, fodder and green manure; pigeon pea is not a green-manure crop (UPSC 2012 key).
Jaya, Padma and Krishna are improved (HYV) rice varieties.
Bahar is a pigeon pea (arhar) variety, like Amar, Azad, Malaviya Vikas and Paras.
source: printed explanation (UPPCS Mains 2013); standard arhar variety lists

x: UPAS-120 is an early-maturing arhar variety, so it fits a double crop with wheat; Bahar is a long-duration arhar.
Rust (black, brown and yellow) is a wheat disease; blast is a rice disease and tikka a groundnut disease.
Barani Deep is an upland rice (paddy) variety of NDUAT Faizabad, like Narendra Shushk Samrat.
source: printed explanation (UPPCS Mains 2013), printed key, not verified

x: Cobalt is needed by Rhizobium for nitrogen fixation in pulse root nodules (and for vitamin B12).
Lobia (cowpea) is the printed key for newly improved dry land: it is drought hardy and grows fast. If the Hindi original meant newly reclaimed usar (sodic) land, dhaincha is the standard choice.
source: printed key, not verified (UPPCS Mains 2008); vikaspedia ऊसर सुधार
evidence: hi.vikaspedia.in ऊसर सुधार (dhaincha for usar reclamation)
dispute: Printed key / book: Lobia (newly improved arid land). If the Hindi original meant newly reclaimed usar (sodic) land, dhaincha (Sesbania) is the standard green manure (vikaspedia, ऊसर सुधार).

x: The Azolla-Anabaena biofertiliser is used in rice fields.
UP-308 is a dwarf wheat variety.
Triticale is a man-made cross of wheat (Triticum) and rye (Secale).
Azolla (with Anabaena) is a biofertiliser; urea and potassium are chemical fertilisers, neem is a biopesticide.

from_notes_src: app notes 4:81 (sub 10); NextGen Indian Economy 20 p.6
x: Kalyan Sona is a high-yielding wheat variety of the Green Revolution.
source: app notes 4:81 (sub 10); NextGen Indian Economy 20 p.6

x: Bt seed carries a Bacillus thuringiensis gene against bollworm; Bt cotton is India's only approved GM crop.
Sunhemp (sanai) is the common green-manure crop, ploughed in to enrich the soil; wheat, cotton and rice are not green manures.
source: TNAU agritech green manuring; printed explanation

x: Hansa, Jaya and Padma are rice varieties; Jawala (Jwala) is not a rice variety (it is a chilli variety).
Pusa RH-10 is IARI's superfine aromatic hybrid basmati rice; Pusa Basmati-1 and the Pusa Sugandh lines are non-hybrid varieties.
source: IARI variety release records; printed explanation

x: The book's table puts cow pea highest in nitrogen (0.49%), ahead of sunhemp 0.43%, dhaincha 0.42% and guar 0.34% (fresh weight).
source: printed key, not verified (UPPCS Mains 2016 book table); agritech.tnau.ac.in green manuring nutrient content
evidence: phytojournal 2018 SP-7-1 (sunhemp highest N, then cowpea, dhaincha)
dispute: Book key / most guides: cow pea (0.49% N, fresh weight). Strictly, other trials and TNAU tables rank sunhemp highest (dry-matter N about 3.2%, ahead of cowpea and dhaincha).

x: Shaktiman-1 and Shaktiman-2 are maize hybrids. They are quality-protein maize from normal breeding, not GM crops, but maize is the only fit.
Pusa Sindhu Ganga (HD 2967) is an IARI wheat variety.
Pusa Sugandh-5 is an aromatic basmati-type rice variety from IARI.

from_notes_src: app notes 4:81 (sub 10); UPSC CSE 2013 official key
x: Nostoc is a nitrogen-fixing blue-green alga used as a biofertiliser; Agaricus is a mushroom and Spirogyra a green alga that does not fix nitrogen (UPSC 2013 key).
source: app notes 4:81 (sub 10); UPSC CSE 2013 official key

x: Sharbati Sonora was made at IARI (1967) by gamma-ray mutation of the Mexican wheat Sonora-64. Sonora-64 itself is a conventionally bred CIMMYT variety.
source: byjus.com question on Swaminathan's amber-seeded mutant wheat
evidence: printed explanation itself says the mutation was done on Sonora-64
dispute: Printed key: Sonora-64 (the parent). Strictly, the induced-mutation variety is Sharbati Sonora, the gamma-ray mutant of Sonora-64 (IARI 1967).

x: India, with about 1.19 billion subscribers (TRAI, Sept 2024), is the world's second-largest telecom market, so statement 1 is right. China is the largest, so statement 2 is wrong.
source: TRAI PR (subscription data 30 Sep 2024); DoT/Economic Survey 2024-25 (India second-largest telecom market)
dispute: Printed key: Both 1 and 2. Strictly only 1 is correct: India is second to China (TRAI, DoT, Economic Survey 2024-25).

x: Intended pairs: maize and rice are kharif crops, sugarcane is perennial and sunflower is rabi in AP. List II as printed seems garbled (Kharif printed twice), so option A only fits if sugarcane takes 'Perennial' and rice takes 'Kharif'.
source: printed key, not verified; Rocket Indian Geography p.80 (crop–season table)

x: Printed key: monocropping – rice (delta paddy), mixed cropping – sorghum, crop rotation – cotton, intercropping – sugarcane (short crops between rows). The pairing is loose; no other option is closer.
source: printed key, not verified; app notes 4:81 (sub 7)

x: Peanut (groundnut) is a legume with two seed leaves, so it is a dicot; wheat, rice and maize are grasses (monocots).
